the two relaxation times are the evidence of the two-stage transport process, and the two-stage transport is the result of the proton transfer in the hydrogen-bonds and the rotation of the SeO 4 2− anions.

the superionic phase transition in Rb 3 (HSeO 4 ), as well as in many other proton conducting systems, is a two-step process, in which the proton is first transferred within the hydrogen bonds and then jumps from one hydrogen bond to the next one.
the superionic phase transition in the studied crystals is a consequence of the proton transfer and rotational hopping in the system with a strong hydrogen bond and the polaron effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two relaxation processes in the superionic Rb 3 (H 1 − x D x )(SeO 4 2 ) 2 crystals are the consequence of the two-stage transport of the protons within the hydrogen bonds.
the proton transport in the hydrogen-bounded system is not only due to the proton transfer within the hydrogen bond but also due to the rotational motion of the proton.

the proton transfer within the H-bond and the rotational hopping of the proton are the two main mechanisms of the ionic transport in the Rb 3  H(SeO 3 ) 2  crystal in the superionic high-temperature phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two-stage transport model can be successfully applied for the description of superionic phase transitions in the hydrogen-bounded systems.

in the region of high-temperature superionic phase transition the relaxation spectrum splits into two peaks, and the difference between the mean relaxation times of the fast and slow relaxators corresponds to the proportion between the rate of the rotational hopping of the proton and the rate of proton transfer within hydrogen bonds.
the two-stage transport is a common feature of the hydrogen-bonding systems.
